capabilities: Bind multi-key character sequences to Obsidian commands
Open a key sequence menu palette that executes commands without Enter
Configure sequence-to-command mappings in a TAB-separated text file
Insert command IDs and names for configuration
Integrate with a vim input method switching plugin for temporary English input
extras: Config file uses TAB separators, which the author notes are awkward to type inside Obsidian; the README recommends typing TAB in another editor and pasting. Version 2.1.0's IME integration is optional and degrades gracefully if the provider plugin is missing.
intentEvidence: It already support key sequence shortcut in editor VIM mode. Then why do I create Key Sequence Shortcut plugin?
motivation: The author loves the vimrc-support plugin but created this because key sequences were unavailable outside VIM mode, for non-VIM users, on mobile, and in preview mode.
problem: Single-keystroke hotkeys like Ctrl-j are hard to memorize in numbers, and existing key-sequence support only works inside VIM editor mode.

relations.evidence: This plugin is inspired by Vim multi-key shortcut and VSpaceCode.
I love vimrc-support plugin so much and I am using it literally everyday.
If an enabled, compatible Vim Input Method Memory plugin (vim-input-method-memory) is available, the palette waits
A compatible legacy installation with ID obsidian-vim-im-switch-plugin is also supported
Chorded hotkeys - Support character sequence as hotkey.
support arbitrary hotkey sequences, so you can use key sequence like "Alt-b Ctrl-a p h w"

summary: Key-sequence hotkey plugin that runs Obsidian commands from short typed character sequences in a palette, configured in a text file.
